title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 seeks to protect U.S.-developed AI models by making it illegal to copy or use them without permission, with the aim of discouraging unauthorized theft. It establishes penalties and enforcement mechanisms for those who violate the law, encouraging companies to secure their AI technologies and uphold intellectual property rights.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to stop companies from unfairly raising AI product prices or manipulating wages in the AI sector. It would set new rules and penalties to protect consumers and workers from exploitative practices and promote fair competition.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a federal framework for studying how artificial intelligence is used in judicial settings and for monitoring its impact on justice. It creates independent review boards, sets standards for transparency and fairness, and requires ongoing data collection to ensure AI tools in courts serve the public interest.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 sets rules and offers support so that small businesses can use AI safely and responsibly, making sure they follow federal privacy and security laws. It also creates grants, training programs, and oversight mechanisms to help small companies adopt AI while keeping their operations ethical and compliant.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard consumers against misleading or deceptive artificial intelligence practices. It establishes clear rules and transparency requirements for AI systems, ensuring that users can identify and understand when they are interacting with AI and what information it may be manipulating.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act proposes a national framework to guide AI research and use, setting uniform standards for safety, privacy, and ethics across the country. It also calls for federal oversight, funding, and partnerships with industry and academia to keep the U.S. competitive in AI technology while addressing workforce and societal impacts.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 is a proposed law designed to regulate the use and development of AI by setting federal standards for assessing and mitigating risks. It requires organizations to conduct risk analyses, implement safety safeguards, and report any AI-related incidents to protect public safety, privacy, and economic interests.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This act seeks to boost the development and use of AI technologies in the financial services sector by establishing a supportive regulatory framework. It encourages innovation while also outlining safeguards to protect consumers and maintain market stability.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act is a proposed law that aims to strengthen AI research capabilities at historically black colleges and universities. It proposes to allocate resources, establish partnerships, and promote leadership roles for HBCU researchers in the AI field.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 mandates that schools teach students the fundamentals of artificial intelligence, including its benefits, risks, and ethical use. It also provides funding and professional development for teachers, sets standards for curriculum implementation, and establishes metrics to evaluate school readiness for AI integration.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to shield users from misleading or deceptive AI-generated content by mandating clear disclosure of AI usage. It imposes penalties on companies that mislead consumers about the nature or capabilities of AI systems, ensuring greater transparency and accountability.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law aimed at governing the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence models to promote transparency, safety, and accountability. It requires companies to disclose model capabilities, conduct impact assessments, and establish safeguards against harmful outcomes.

title: SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.
summary: The SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026 requires the Small Business Administration to gather and share information about how small businesses are using artificial intelligence. It aims to increase transparency, help lawmakers understand AI’s impact, and guide future AI‑related policy decisions.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to regulate how artificial intelligence is developed and used, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It aims to set clear standards, enforce oversight, and protect consumers while encouraging ethical AI practices.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 mandates that companies conduct regular impact assessments of their AI systems, focusing on fairness, accuracy, and potential harms to consumers. It requires transparent reporting, independent audits, and imposes penalties for non‑compliance to promote responsible AI deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 establishes legal protections for individuals interacting with AI systems, ensuring that AI technology must respect civil liberties such as privacy, non-discrimination, and freedom of expression. It requires developers and users to implement safeguards and accountability mechanisms, and provides a framework for oversight and redress if AI practices infringe on civil rights.

title: To prohibit the manufacture and conveyance of certain products for children that incorporate an artificial intelligence chatbot, and for other purposes.
action: Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR H3000-3001)
summary: The policy bans the manufacturing and selling of child‑oriented products that include an AI chatbot, aiming to protect children from potentially harmful AI interactions. It also covers other related activities, though the specific details are not provided.

title: To codify Executive Order 14319 (relating to preventing woke AI in the Federal Government).
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The policy formalizes Executive Order 14319, setting rules for how the federal government must use artificial‑intelligence systems. It focuses on preventing political or ideological bias—often called “woke” bias—by requiring transparent, accountable, and neutral AI design and deployment.

title: To amend the Public Health Service Act to update quality standards for mammography facilities for the use of AI systems, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill amends the Public Health Service Act to revise the quality standards that mammography facilities must meet, specifically addressing how AI systems can be integrated into breast imaging. It also includes related provisions aimed at improving patient safety, ensuring accurate diagnostics, and clarifying regulatory responsibilities for healthcare providers.

title: American Leadership in AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committees on Energy and Commerce, Agriculture, Oversight and Government Reform, Education and Workforce, the Judiciary, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American Leadership in AI Act is designed to keep the United States at the cutting edge of artificial‑intelligence technology. It proposes increased federal support for AI research, workforce training, and ethical standards, while encouraging international cooperation and protecting national security interests.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 is intended to boost AI learning and research across schools and universities by providing new funding and setting clearer curriculum goals. It encourages partnerships between the NSF, academia, and industry to train students and researchers for future AI careers, helping the country stay competitive in the field.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to boost the export of AI technologies by offering incentives and simplifying regulatory hurdles for companies. It seeks to position the country as a global AI leader by supporting research, development, and international partnerships while managing export controls.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act seeks to shield families from higher household bills caused by the energy use of AI data centers. It proposes regulations to curb or offset the extra power costs from large AI infrastructures so families aren’t disproportionately burdened.

title: Condemning antisemitism in all its forms, including the proliferation and amplification of antisemitic content on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms, urging robust, transparent safeguards for AI, and recognizing stakeholders working to counter this threat.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy declares a firm condemnation of antisemitism, particularly its spread and amplification through AI platforms. It urges the implementation of robust, transparent safeguards for AI and acknowledges stakeholders working to counter this threat.
